questions.title: Catalysed chlorination of benzene — mechanism features
questions.prompt: Benzene reacts with Cl₂ using a halogen carrier. Select the two catalyst equations and mechanism features. Either a consistent AlCl₃ or FeCl₃ pair is allowed.
questions.assessmentNotice: Recognition practice · Choose one option for each part. All features within a part are needed for its single mark. Parts are marked independently.

components.label: Choose a complete pair: electrophile generation AND catalyst regeneration
Choose the arrow for electrophilic attack
Choose the electron movement that restores aromaticity

questions.feedback: The halogen carrier generates the electrophile and is regenerated. Both equations together earn one mark. The arene π electrons donate to the electrophile; the positive chlorine is the destination, not the source. Attack temporarily breaks aromaticity. The attacked carbon retains H and gains Cl; the positive charge is delocalised over the remaining π-system. The C–H bond pair returns to the π-system as H+ is lost; the C–Cl bond remains. Recognition practice: each complete feature group earns one mark. This is not freehand mechanism drawing or examiner error-carried-forward marking.

misconceptions.mp-eas-m1-1: The halogen carrier generates the electrophile and is regenerated. Both equations together earn one mark. Check: Cl2 + AlCl3 → Cl+ + AlCl4−. H+ + AlCl4− → AlCl3 + HCl. Alternatively, both corresponding FeCl3/FeCl4− equations are correct. Do not mix aluminium and iron species between the pair.
